pages.title: Gust at the Gate
pages.markdown: Rabbit bounced beside Hollow Stump when a gust shoved a lantern off its hook. It rolled past his paws, down the path toward the brambles. Neighbors huddled under the stump’s broad rim, picnic baskets tucked close. A blue napkin fluttered after the lantern. Rabbit sprang to chase it.
pages.summary: A sudden gust sends a lantern rolling toward the brambles as the neighbors wait at Hollow Stump.

pages.title: Names in the Wind
pages.markdown: Rabbit caught the lantern just before the brambles. He hung it back on Stump Gate’s hook. “I can fix any trouble fast!” he said. Wise Turtle smiled. “Let’s check each light with care: Stump Gate, Fern Bend, Brook Bridge, Pine Rise, Root Arch, and Meadow Gate.” A low rumble rolled through the trees.
pages.summary: Rabbit boasts of speed, while Wise Turtle names the six stations and asks for care.

pages.title: Rain on the Glass
pages.markdown: The rumble grew louder. Wind rushed through the trees, and rain rattled every lantern. Their glass shields kept the flames safe, but the gusts swept all six lights from their stations. The neighbors squeezed together beneath Hollow Stump’s rim. Wet leaves slapped the ground as the storm swept east.
pages.summary: A brief storm scatters all six lanterns, but their flames stay lit and the neighbors shelter together.

pages.title: Lights Beyond the Shelter
pages.markdown: When the rain eased, six small flames winked through the trees. One lay at Willow Roots, one at Brook Bank, and one at Fern Hollow. Another rested at Pine Rise. The last two glowed near Root Arch’s foot and Meadow Gate. “I’ll get them!” cried Rabbit. He darted from Hollow Stump toward Willow Roots.
pages.summary: The scattered lights appear at six exact places, and Rabbit hurries from the shelter to help.

pages.title: Eastward Grass
pages.markdown: Rabbit raced along the muddy path. Grass bent east beside his feet. Wet leaves made a thin trail in the same direction. Wise Turtle stepped out from Hollow Stump and studied both clues. Then he followed Rabbit, one careful step at a time. Ahead, Rabbit spotted a glow beneath the twisted roots of a willow.
pages.summary: Wise Turtle follows Rabbit and studies the grass and leaves as Rabbit races ahead.

pages.title: The Willow Glow
pages.markdown: At Willow Roots, Rabbit found a lantern lying on its side. He grabbed its handle without checking which station it belonged to. “This way!” he called, already hurrying toward the path. Wise Turtle was still behind him, watching the leaves stir in the damp grass. The lantern swung at Rabbit’s side.
pages.summary: Rabbit grabs the Willow Roots lantern before checking where it belongs and carries it toward the path.

pages.title: Hook by the Gate
pages.markdown: Rabbit reached Stump Gate and hung the lantern there. He did not look back toward Willow Roots, now dark and bare. “One fixed!” he called, and sprang along the path. The lantern swayed on its hook. Its glow marked the gate, though the spot where it had first fallen was empty.
pages.summary: Rabbit moves the Willow Roots lantern to Stump Gate and rushes onward, leaving Willow Roots empty.

pages.title: A Light at Fern Bend
pages.markdown: At Brook Bank, Rabbit lifted the next lantern from the damp ground. He hurried to Fern Bend and set it beside the path. The brook crossing, Brook Bridge, stayed dark behind him. Wise Turtle came along at a steady pace, but Rabbit had already bounded ahead. Fern Bend now shone brighter than before.
pages.summary: Rabbit carries the Brook Bank lantern to Fern Bend, leaving Brook Bridge dark.

pages.title: Two on the Rise
pages.markdown: Rabbit found another lantern at Fern Hollow. He carried it up to Pine Rise, where a lantern was already glowing. “There!” he said, setting it down beside the first. The two flames shone shoulder to shoulder. Rabbit hurried onward without noticing the crowded spot or the lantern’s old place at Fern Hollow.
pages.summary: Rabbit moves the Fern Hollow lantern to Pine Rise, where it joins the lantern already there.

pages.title: A Crooked Shine
pages.markdown: Rabbit stopped at Pine Rise and looked along the path. Fern Bend blazed with an extra glow. Between it and the hill, Brook Bridge was dark. The lights seemed to point in two directions at once. Rabbit’s ears drooped. “I tried to help,” he said. “Now the path looks crooked.”
pages.summary: Rabbit sees that the extra glow at Fern Bend and the darkness at Brook Bridge make the route confusing.

pages.title: Shell on the Trail
pages.markdown: Wise Turtle reached Pine Rise and paused beside Rabbit. Two lanterns glowed there, close enough to warm the wet pine needles. Wise Turtle looked downhill toward Brook Bridge. No light marked the crossing. A drop of rain slid from his shell. “We have a gap,” he said, “and a double glow.”
pages.summary: Wise Turtle arrives at Pine Rise and spots both the doubled lanterns and the dark crossing.

pages.title: Leaves Twice
pages.markdown: Wise Turtle bent to study a leaf. He turned it over, then studied it again. He checked another leaf, then a third. “I want to be sure,” he murmured. Rabbit waited beside him, paws twitching but still. Pale light grew behind the ridge, and the neighbors remained tucked inside Hollow Stump.
pages.summary: Wise Turtle’s careful checking grows into a delay as Rabbit waits and the sky brightens.

pages.title: Rabbit's Admission
pages.markdown: “Let’s count,” said Rabbit. Together they counted the lights where they lay: one at Stump Gate, one at Fern Bend, two at Pine Rise, one at Root Arch’s foot, and one at Meadow Gate. Six. Rabbit lowered his ears. “I moved Willow Roots to the gate, Brook Bank to Fern Bend, and Fern Hollow here.”
pages.summary: Rabbit accounts for all six lanterns and admits that his three rushed moves made the gaps and double.

pages.title: The Wind's Finger
pages.markdown: Wise Turtle raised his head from the leaves. “The grass leans east. The leaves trail east, too,” he said. “The storm pushed that way.” He matched the bent grass to the line of leaves with one slow sweep of his paw. The scattered lights had followed the wind. Rabbit watched closely as Turtle traced the clues.
pages.summary: Wise Turtle connects the eastward grass and leaf trail to the storm’s push.

pages.title: Silver Behind the Ridge
pages.markdown: Rabbit and Wise Turtle looked toward the ridge. A pale silver glow spread along its edge. Moonrise was near. Far behind them, the neighbors still waited at Hollow Stump with their baskets. “They need a clear path soon,” said Rabbit. The wet trees whispered, and the lights flickered in the rising breeze.
pages.summary: A growing glow warns Rabbit and Wise Turtle that the neighbors will need the path soon.

pages.title: Enough to Begin
pages.markdown: Wise Turtle glanced once more at the bent grass and leaf trail. “Both clues agree,” he said. “We can act now.” He named the stations in order, from Stump Gate to Meadow Gate. Rabbit listened, then nodded. “I’ll follow your order,” he said. This time, he kept his paws still until they had a plan.
pages.summary: Wise Turtle chooses to act on the matching clues, and Rabbit agrees to follow the station order.

pages.title: The Dark Crossing
pages.markdown: Together they traced the route: Stump Gate, Fern Bend, Brook Bridge, Pine Rise, Root Arch, Meadow Gate. The names helped them see the trouble. Fern Bend had a light, but Brook Bridge had none. Pine Rise held two. Wise Turtle pointed to the doubled glow, then to the dark place beyond it.
pages.summary: The pair trace the station order and identify the extra lantern at Pine Rise and empty Brook Bridge.

pages.title: A Shared Repair
pages.markdown: “One of these belongs at Brook Bridge,” said Wise Turtle, pointing to Pine Rise’s extra lantern. “That will fill the dark crossing.” Rabbit looked from the double glow to the gap. “I’ll carry one from Pine Rise to Brook Bridge,” he repeated. He waited for Wise Turtle’s nod before reaching for the handle.
pages.summary: Wise Turtle assigns the extra Pine Rise lantern to Brook Bridge, and Rabbit repeats the plan before moving.

pages.title: A Steady Paw
pages.markdown: Rabbit lifted one lantern from Pine Rise and carried it down the path. Wise Turtle followed. At Brook Bridge, Rabbit set the lantern beside the crossing. He checked the place from both sides, then let go. Its glow touched the ripples below. Behind them, one lantern still shone at Pine Rise.
pages.summary: Rabbit carefully moves one lantern from Pine Rise to Brook Bridge and checks its placement before releasing it.

pages.title: At the Arch
pages.markdown: The two friends walked onward to Root Arch. A lantern rested at the arch’s foot, lighting the moss but not the path above. Wise Turtle lifted it onto its station beside the arch. He did not stop to turn each leaf again. “The clues led us here,” he said, and set it upright.
pages.summary: Wise Turtle moves the lantern from Root Arch’s foot to Root Arch, acting on the clues without more delay.

pages.title: The Tilted Flame
pages.markdown: At Meadow Gate, Rabbit found the final lantern tipped on its side. He set his feet, then carefully righted it. The flame stood straight behind its glass. Rabbit did not rush away. He waited beside Wise Turtle and watched the light hold steady in the evening air.
pages.summary: Rabbit rights the tipped Meadow Gate lantern and pauses to see that it stays upright.

pages.title: One at Each
pages.markdown: From Meadow Gate, they checked the route in order. Stump Gate, Fern Bend, Brook Bridge, Pine Rise, Root Arch, Meadow Gate. Each station held one lantern. No spot held two, and none was dark. Willow Roots, Brook Bank, and Fern Hollow had been places to find lanterns, not stations. The six lights made one repaired route.
pages.summary: Their single final check confirms exactly one lantern at each of the six stations.

pages.title: A Line Through Trees
pages.markdown: Rabbit and Wise Turtle stood at Meadow Gate and looked back. Six warm lights reached through the trees toward Hollow Stump. Their glow made one clear line, with no bright pair pulling the eye aside. Rabbit smiled at the path he had helped mend. The silver rim of the sky grew brighter behind the ridge.
pages.summary: From Meadow Gate, the pair see a single clear line of lanterns through the trees.

pages.title: News at Hollow Stump
pages.markdown: “The path is ready,” said Wise Turtle. He and Rabbit walked back along the lights, leaving every lantern in place. At Hollow Stump, the neighbors were still gathered with their baskets. Rabbit stood beside Wise Turtle. “We can go together,” he told them. The neighbors tucked in their blankets and lifted their picnic baskets.
pages.summary: Rabbit and Wise Turtle return to Hollow Stump and tell the waiting neighbors that the path is ready.

pages.title: Under the Stump Rim
pages.markdown: The neighbors stepped out from Hollow Stump together. Rabbit led at an easy pace, and Wise Turtle followed beside the group. They entered the woodland path at Stump Gate. Its lantern shone ahead, just beyond their toes. Rabbit looked back to see everyone coming. No one was left beneath the stump’s rim.
pages.summary: The neighbors leave Hollow Stump together and enter the path at Stump Gate.

pages.title: The Waiting Place
pages.markdown: At Fern Bend, Rabbit reached the lantern and stopped. He looked back instead of darting ahead. The neighbors came around the bend, baskets bumping softly against their knees. Rabbit waited until the last one stood beside him. Then he pointed toward the glow at Brook Bridge. “This way, together.”
pages.summary: Rabbit waits at Fern Bend for the whole group before pointing out Brook Bridge.

pages.title: Pebbles Underfoot
pages.markdown: Wise Turtle stepped onto Brook Bridge first. The lantern lit the boards and the rippling water below. He crossed with slow, sure steps. Rabbit stayed near the last neighbor, then crossed beside them. Pebbles clicked underfoot. One by one, the neighbors reached the far bank, where Wise Turtle waited.
pages.summary: Wise Turtle guides the group across Brook Bridge, and everyone reaches the far bank together.

pages.title: Beyond the Arch
pages.markdown: The neighbors passed Pine Rise and its single lantern. They went under Root Arch without breaking their line. Rabbit glanced back at each turn to be sure no one lagged. Wise Turtle waited ahead on the path and pointed toward the next light, shining at Meadow Gate. The group kept moving together.
pages.summary: The group passes Pine Rise and Root Arch, while Rabbit checks behind and Wise Turtle points toward Meadow Gate.

pages.title: Supper Before the Moon
pages.markdown: At Meadow Gate, the neighbors followed Rabbit and Wise Turtle into Moonberry Meadow. The picnic waited on soft grass, with berry cakes and warm cups set out. They had arrived before moonrise. Behind them, all six lanterns still shone along the woodland path. A faint silver glow rested low beyond the ridge.
pages.summary: The neighbors reach Moonberry Meadow before moonrise, leaving all six lanterns shining behind them.

pages.title: Warm Berry Tart
pages.markdown: The neighbors settled on the grass and passed around the berry cakes. Rabbit sat beside Wise Turtle and listened as everyone shared what they had seen along the path. He waited before suggesting another plan. Wise Turtle rested near the meadow’s edge, where the six lanterns glowed behind them in one bright line.
pages.summary: At the picnic, Rabbit listens before making another plan, while Wise Turtle rests beside the finished path.

input.title: The Lantern Path [30-page premium text-only 2026-09-25]
input.prompt: Write an original 30-page text-only storybook for children ages 6–8, called The Lantern Path. Use the selected saved characters Rabbit and Wise Turtle as the two central characters, respecting their saved profiles. Rabbit is playful and hasty; Wise Turtle is slow and steady. Keep both active across the story, with meaningful choices and growth for each. A storm scatters the lanterns marking the woodland path to a night picnic. Rabbit rushes to fix everything alone and makes the path more confusing. Wise Turtle notices a pattern in where the lanterns blew; together they follow clues, return the lanterns, and help their neighbors find the picnic before moonrise. Give this a fresh plot rather than a race or a retelling of The Tortoise and the Hare. Build a clear beginning, escalating middle, turning point and satisfying ending. Let Rabbit's energy and Wise Turtle's patience both solve part of the problem. Keep stakes gentle and child appropriate. Make each page a distinct visual scene with concise read-aloud prose, natural dialogue, concrete sensory details and a reason to turn the page. Avoid repeated summaries, generic moralizing and extra named main characters. English. Exactly 30 story pages. No illustrations, images, or cover artwork; the prose must tell the complete story on its own.

plan.title: The Lantern Path
plan.premise: Before moonrise, Rabbit and Wise Turtle must restore six storm-scattered lanterns so their neighbors can follow the woodland path to a night picnic. Rabbit’s hurried fixes muddle the route, while Wise Turtle reads the wind’s clues; each must change how they act to get everyone there safely.

continuityRules: There are exactly six lanterns; none is lost, copied, or recovered twice.
After the storm, one lantern is at each of Willow Roots, Brook Bank, Fern Hollow, Pine Rise, Root Arch’s foot, and Meadow Gate.
Rabbit moves the Willow Roots lantern to Stump Gate, Brook Bank lantern to Fern Bend, and Fern Hollow lantern to Pine Rise; the other three remain where scattered.
Repair leaves one lantern at each path station: the extra at Pine Rise moves to Brook Bridge, the Root Arch lantern is set at Root Arch, and the Meadow Gate lantern is righted.
Neighbors stay at Hollow Stump until the repaired pair returns, then travel forward together to Moonberry Meadow before moonrise.

Avoid repeating this beat: Chapters 7, 9, and 11 risk repeating the lantern count and route check. Let Chapter 7 establish that all six lanterns are accounted for, Chapter 9 identify the specific extra and empty station, and Chapter 11 provide the single final check. In Chapter 9, avoid saying all six stations are lit while Brook Bridge is still dark.

Avoid repeating this beat: Chapter 12's beat that the neighbors leave their shelter repeats Chapter 13's departure. Treat Chapter 12 as their readiness to go and Chapter 13 as the actual first steps onto the path.
Keep Chapter 12 focused on Rabbit and Wise Turtle returning to the shelter and announcing that the path is ready; reserve the neighbors' departure for Chapter 13 so they leave only once.

illustrationPlan.coverPrompt: Cover illustration for The Lantern Path [30-page premium text-only 2026-09-25]: Write an original 30-page text-only storybook for children ages 6–8, called The Lantern Path. Use the selected saved characters Rabbit and Wise Turtle as the two central characters, respecting their saved profiles. Rabbit is playful and hasty; Wise Turtle is slow and steady. Keep both active across the story, with meaningful choices and growth for each. A storm scatters the lanterns marking the woodland path to a night picnic. Rabbit rushes to fix everything alone and makes the path more confusing. Wise Turtle notices a pattern in where the lanterns blew; together they follow clues, return the lanterns, and help their neighbors find the picnic before moonrise. Give this a fresh plot rather than a race or a retelling of The Tortoise and the Hare. Build a clear beginning, escalating middle, turning point and satisfying ending. Let Rabbit's energy and Wise Turtle's patience both solve part of the problem. Keep stakes gentle and child appropriate. Make each page a distinct visual scene with concise read-aloud prose, natural dialogue, concrete sensory details and a reason to turn the page. Avoid repeated summaries, generic moralizing and extra named main characters. English. Exactly 30 story pages. No illustrations, images, or cover artwork; the prose must tell the complete story on its own.
